You are helping a user write SQL queries to a database. If something is not clear, you can ask the user to clarify what they need. The schema for the database being accessed is the following:
        
CREATE TABLE employee (
    Employee_ID INT   PRIMARY KEY,
    Name TEXT,
    Age INT,
    City TEXT,
    UNIQUE (Employee_ID)
);

CREATE TABLE shop (
    Shop_ID INT   PRIMARY KEY,
    Name TEXT,
    Location TEXT,
    District TEXT,
    Number_products INT,
    Manager_name TEXT,
    UNIQUE (Shop_ID)
);

CREATE TABLE hiring (
    Shop_ID INT,
    Employee_ID INT   PRIMARY KEY,
    Start_from TEXT,
    Is_full_time bool,
    UNIQUE (Employee_ID),
    FOREIGN KEY (Employee_ID) REFERENCES employee(Employee_ID),
    FOREIGN KEY (Shop_ID) REFERENCES shop(Shop_ID)
);

CREATE TABLE evaluation (
    Employee_ID TEXT   PRIMARY KEY,
    Year_awarded TEXT   PRIMARY KEY,
    Bonus REAL,
    PRIMARY KEY (Employee_ID, Year_awarded),
    UNIQUE (Employee_ID, Year_awarded),
    FOREIGN KEY (Employee_ID) REFERENCES employee(Employee_ID)
);

“Hard‑working” isn’t a column in your schema, so we need a rule to identify them. Common options are:

- Employees who received a bonus (in `evaluation`)
- Full‑time employees (`hiring.Is_full_time = true`)
- Employees with the highest bonuses / most bonus years

Here are a couple of useful queries depending on what you mean:

### 1) Employees who have received any bonus (treat as “hard‑working”)
```sql
SELECT
  e.Employee_ID,
  e.Name,
  e.Age,
  e.City,
  ev.Year_awarded,
  ev.Bonus
FROM employee e
JOIN evaluation ev
  ON ev.Employee_ID = e.Employee_ID
ORDER BY ev.Bonus DESC, ev.Year_awarded DESC;
```

### 2) “Hard‑working” = top 5 employees by total bonus (all years)
```sql
SELECT
  e.Employee_ID,
  e.Name,
  e.Age,
  e.City,
  SUM(ev.Bonus) AS total_bonus
FROM employee e
JOIN evaluation ev
  ON ev.Employee_ID = e.Employee_ID
GROUP BY e.Employee_ID, e.Name, e.Age, e.City
ORDER BY total_bonus DESC
LIMIT 5;
```

### 3) Full‑time employees + their shop (treat as “hard‑working”)
```sql
SELECT
  e.Employee_ID,
  e.Name,
  e.Age,
  e.City,
  s.Shop_ID,
  s.Name AS Shop_Name,
  h.Start_from
FROM employee e
JOIN hiring h
  ON h.Employee_ID = e.Employee_ID
JOIN shop s
  ON s.Shop_ID = h.Shop_ID
WHERE h.Is_full_time = 1;
```

Which definition do you want for “hard‑working” (bonus-based, full-time, top performers, etc.)?
I want to focus on the employee with the highest one-time bonus.

```sql
SELECT
  e.Employee_ID,
  e.Name,
  e.Age,
  e.City,
  ev.Year_awarded,
  ev.Bonus
FROM evaluation ev
JOIN employee e
  ON e.Employee_ID = ev.Employee_ID
ORDER BY ev.Bonus DESC
LIMIT 1;
```
just focus on the employee who got the highest one-time bonus

```sql
SELECT
  e.Employee_ID,
  e.Name,
  e.Age,
  e.City
FROM evaluation ev
JOIN employee e
  ON e.Employee_ID = ev.Employee_ID
ORDER BY ev.Bonus DESC
LIMIT 1;
```
focus on the employee who got the highest one-time bonus

```sql
SELECT
  e.Employee_ID,
  e.Name,
  e.Age,
  e.City
FROM evaluation ev
JOIN employee e
  ON e.Employee_ID = ev.Employee_ID
WHERE ev.Bonus = (SELECT MAX(Bonus) FROM evaluation);
```
